elements.problem: Split into 8 parts. Infection: 'Infected ulcer of skin' OR 'Local infection of wound' (acceptable, but the page defines infection by signs a health worker records: redness, warmth or swelling around the ulcer; 'Wound cellulitis' disorder exists and is closer). SBP < 80 mmHg: correct. Pulse > 100 bpm: correct. Temperature ≥ 38 °C: correct. Confused: 'Acute confusion', correct. Blisters: 'Blister of skin', correct. Crepitus: 'Subcutaneous crepitus', correct (matches the footnote). Severe pain: 'Severe pain', correct. Logic is 'infection AND any of', matching the page.

elements.problem: 'Lower leg or foot' is encoded as ulcer at 'Structure of lower limb from knee to ankle' OR 'Foot structure'. 'Ankle region structure' is a descendant of neither (its parents are 'Structure of ankle and/or foot' and 'Structure of joint region of lower limb'), so an ankle/malleolar ulcer in a mobile patient, the classic venous-ulcer site, fails the lower-leg-or-foot branch and gets no arterial, venous or diabetic diagnosis. 'Structure of ankle and/or foot' or adding the ankle site would fix it. The 'No' branch (not lower leg/foot → ask-about box) has no diagnosis on the page, so nothing more is needed there.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable arterial (ischaemic) ulcer (APC 2026 page 90) / Diagnose probable venous ulcer (APC 2026 page 90) / Diagnose probable diabetic ulcer (APC 2026 page 90)
rule_level_problems.problem: Lower-leg-or-foot gate is ulcer @ 'Structure of lower limb from knee to ankle' OR 'Foot structure'; 'Ankle region structure' (also checked as a pressure site) descends from neither, so an ankle/malleolar ulcer in a mobile patient fails all three lower-limb branches and gets no diagnosis. Use 'Structure of ankle and/or foot' or add the ankle site to the gate.

rule_level_problems.rule: Urgent: skin ulcer or non-healing wound with infection and systemic or severe signs
rule_level_problems.problem: The infection gate is only 'Infected ulcer of skin' / 'Local infection of wound'; the page defines infection by the bedside signs (surrounding redness/warmth/swelling), none of which is checked for. A health worker who records redness and swelling plus pulse 120 will not trigger Urgent unless they also code an infection diagnosis. 'Wound cellulitis' (disorder) is a closer, recordable concept.

'Non-healing wound' is 'Wound, non-healed' (morphologic abnormality) inside clinical_finding; the disorder 'Chronic wound' exists. And the cause-identification flowchart only uses site-qualified 'Skin ulcer', so a patient recorded with a non-healing wound never reaches any of the four 'likely' diagnoses.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable arterial (ischaemic) ulcer (APC 2026 page 90) / Diagnose probable venous ulcer (APC 2026 page 90) / Diagnose probable diabetic ulcer (APC 2026 page 90)
rule_level_problems.problem: The not-pressure-ulcer branch requires recorded absence (no …) of bedridden AND wheelchair, or of all eight site ulcers. The De Morgan logic is correct, but if the health worker leaves the bedridden/wheelchair items unrecorded the downstream branches cannot fire. This matches the house pattern for No branches, so it is noted, not an error.

summary: Most consequential: the 'lower leg or foot' gate omits the ankle (Ankle region structure is under neither lower-leg nor foot), so ankle/malleolar ulcers, the classic venous site, get no arterial/venous/diabetic diagnosis. The infected-ulcer Urgent rule hinges on a coded infection diagnosis rather than the page's own signs (red/warm/swollen surrounding skin). Otherwise the red box, the critical limb ischaemia rule and the four flowchart branches are encoded faithfully with sound negation of earlier No answers.
